issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may overturn an acquittal only where the trial court’s findings are perverse or compelling circumstances justify interference, bearing in mind the strengthened presumption of innocence and preferring the trial court’s view when two views are possible.

An accused’s criminal liability for murder must be assessed on the basis of that accused’s individual acts, and participation limited to conduct such as inflicting simple injuries does not ordinarily justify conviction for murder.
An appellate court that convicts an accused after overturning an acquittal must give the accused an opportunity to be heard on the appropriate sentence before imposing it.
